Hi @YassineYousfi, thanks for running the eval! Quick note on a CUDA vs CPU runner mismatch that meaningfully changes the score for this submission:

The eval was triggered on `linux-nvidia-t4` (CUDA / DALI / NVDEC), but I marked **"requires GPU for inflation: no"** specifically because `evaluate.sh` defaults to `--device cpu` (AVVideoDataset / libav) and that's the ground-truth decoder my generator was tuned against. The two ground-truth pipelines use different YUV→RGB matrix coefficients, which shifts SegNet's `argmax` on boundary pixels and thus the per-pair distortion.

For this submission specifically:

- **CPU (AVVideoDataset)**: 0.23 — PoseNet 0.000495, SegNet 0.000272 (my pre-submission CI run on ubuntu-latest: https://github.com/BradyMeighan/comma_video_compression_challenge/actions/runs/25306126756)
- **CUDA (DALI)**: 0.25 — PoseNet 0.000637, SegNet 0.000405 (your run)
Follow-up: looks like CUDA was intended (the other recent submissions all got the same runner). I guess my model just overfit to AVVideoDataset haha.
yeah there is a small hw difference in the decode, I ran all submissions in t4 for a fair comparison.

@YassineYousfi looks like I didn't crack the top 3 but I put together a pretty cool interactive writeup that goes deep on how I built and trained the model and every byte-saving method I used: https://comma-writeup.pages.dev/. Just wanted to make sure you guys see it. Thanks for the fun challenge, hopefully next time I'll come up with something better ;)
